question: A payment call `POST /charges` times out after 10 s. Your retry helper retries it automatically. What can go wrong, and what is the fix?
options: Nothing: a timeout means the charge failed
The first request may have succeeded on the server, so the retry charges twice. Send an idempotency key so the server deduplicates
The retry will always get a 409
Timeouts cannot be retried in Node
explanation: A timeout tells you nothing about whether the server processed the request. Retry non-idempotent writes only with an idempotency key the server honors.

question: After an outage, 5 000 clients retry every 500 ms exactly. What is the likely effect on the recovering service?
options: Synchronized waves of requests (a thundering herd) that can knock it over again; jitter spreads them out
None: fixed delays are the safest
The service rate-limits automatically, so it is fine
explanation: Identical delays keep clients in lockstep. Exponential backoff plus random jitter desynchronizes them.

question: Which response should a retry policy NOT retry?
explanation: Validation errors are deterministic: the same payload fails the same way. Fix the request instead.

question: An AI-generated client wraps an AWS SDK call (which already retries 3 times) in its own retry loop of 5, and the API gateway in front also retries twice. What is the review comment?
options: Good: more retries mean more reliability
Remove the SDK retries because they are hidden
Retries multiply across layers (up to 3 × 4 × 6 = 72 calls per request). Keep retries in one layer and give the others a deadline
Add a fourth layer of retries for safety
explanation: Stacked retries turn a slow dependency into a flood. Know which layer owns retries, and bound the total time with a deadline.
